pathway.title: WEX Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Earnings are large and fee-based but move with the fuel price. Calculated EBITDA was USD 995.0 million in FY2025 on revenue of USD 2,660.8 million, a 37.39% margin, and USD 1,097.8 million over the last twelve months to 2026-09-30. Mobility is 54.46% of nine-month 2026 revenue, and USD 119.0 million of its USD 161.3 million revenue growth came from higher fuel prices, so recent growth is price rather than volume and could reverse. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; calculation C2

Leverage is high on the consolidated measure and moderate on the corporate cut, and the consolidated figure has risen since FY2023. Total debt to EBITDA was 4.19x at the end of FY2023, 4.88x at the end of FY2025 and 4.85x at 2026-09-30, with net debt to EBITDA of 4.31x; excluding the bank and securitization funding of receivables, corporate debt was 3.20x. Creditors of the credit agreement and notes should anchor on the corporate cut while recognising that EBITDA still includes bank earnings. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

Debt service cover is the thinnest metric and has fallen. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.98x in FY2025 against 3.72x in FY2023, and covered accrued financing interest 4.14x in FY2025; the cash-paid measure is conservative because it appears to include interest on bank funding that EBITDA already deducts. Interim cash interest is not printed, so no cover is stated at 2026-09-30. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

Liquidity is adequate on paper but rests on counterparties. The revolver had USD 1,160.5 million undrawn at 2026-09-30 and cash was USD 593.2 million, of which USD 463.0 million sat in WEX Bank, whose FHLB capacity was only USD 14.3 million and whose federal funds lines are uncommitted. The revolver is available only while the covenants are met, so a covenant breach would remove the main committed buffer. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23, 53

Refinancing is a 2028 event, inside 500 days of the cutoff. The Term B-2 Loans of USD 1,364.0 million fall due on 2028-04-01, 500 days from the cutoff, and the Term A-1 Loans and revolver fall due on 2028-01-01, 409 days away, if the early-maturity rule in the credit agreement note applies, or on 2029-05-10 on the annual report's schedule. WEX placed new notes and term loans in March 2025, so market access is demonstrated, but the maturity outcome depends on leverage then. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_wex-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 190; calculation C3

Financial policy is the main constraint. Buybacks of USD 2,016.1 million since 2023 include USD 801.6 million in FY2025, which was 0.80x of adjusted free cash flow of USD 638.0 million and was funded in part by new debt, while nine-month 2026 buybacks were covered 1.92x. USD 740.0 million of authority remains, and equity of USD 1,152.1 million was 7.11% of total assets. Financial foundation shows corporate debt rose by USD 452.5 million over FY2025; Business & governance describes the March 2025 debt as raising corporate debt by USD 1,000.0 million, which is the gross issue, and the net rise was smaller because the same proceeds repaid revolver borrowings. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_wex-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 119, 171, 187–188; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 19, 56, 61; calculation C4; calculation C5

The bank is both the funding advantage and the structural risk. Short-term deposits were USD 6,180.5 million, restricted bank net assets were about 38% of consolidated net assets, and WEX Bank's total capital ratio of 13.01% sat above the 10.00% well-capitalized level. Parent creditors depend on dividends from the bank and on cash outside it, and any loss of deposit or FHLB funding would first hit receivable growth and then the revolver. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 20, 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_wex-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 200; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: The credit strengths are scale, a diversified fee base, earnings that held through FY2023 to FY2025 and policy restraint on dividends. Revenue was USD 2,660.8 million with no customer above 10 percent, no segment above 55% of nine-month revenue, calculated EBITDA between USD 923.3 million and USD 1,007.6 million in the three fiscal years, and adjusted free cash flow of USD 638.0 million in FY2025 and USD 502.8 million in nine months 2026. No dividend has been declared since 2005 and covenant leverage was 2.7x against a 4.75x maximum. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_wex-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 119, 199, 208; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56; calculation C2

The credit weaknesses are leverage tolerance, fuel-price dependence, bank dependence and thin interest cover. Buybacks exceeded adjusted free cash flow in FY2025 and were partly debt-funded, Mobility revenue growth is mostly price, restricted bank net assets are about 38% of consolidated net assets, and cash interest cover fell to 2.98x. The covenant definitions, guarantors and collateral are not established, and no rating or market evidence is supplied. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: WEX issued new debt in March 2025 to fund shareholder returns, not an acquisition: the Seventh Amendment on 2025-03-06 added a USD 450.0 million Term B-3 due 2032-03-06 and the company placed USD 550.0 million of senior unsecured notes at 6.5% due 2033-03-15, with proceeds used primarily to fund the USD 750.0 million tender offer that closed on 2025-03-31 and to repay revolver borrowings. Earlier amendments in 2024 repriced the term loans, raised revolver commitments to USD 1.6 billion and extended maturities, and in 2026 no new debt issue appears in the supplied filings. The one operating transaction is the bp co-branded fleet card program, an asset acquisition for which USD 58.6 million was advanced in 2025 and USD 23.0 million for receivables was paid in the second quarter of 2026. Creditors should read the 2025 financing as raising corporate debt by USD 1,000.0 million for a distribution, partly offset by longer maturities. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wex-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 171, 187–188; 10-K_2024-12-31_wex-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 192–193; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation C5

The step up in FY2025 came from debt raised in March 2025 to fund the share tender offer, and the step up since comes from bank funding of larger receivables: carrying debt rose by USD 462.7 million in nine months while bank and securitization funding rose by USD 537.2 million, so corporate debt fell by USD 74.5 million and the whole increase funds customer receivables. Creditors of the Credit Agreement and Senior Notes should therefore anchor on the corporate cut of 3.20x at 2026-09-30, an analyst split in which EBITDA still includes WEX Bank earnings, which was 3.60x on year-end FY2025 debt of USD 3,586.8 million over FY2025 EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is how little of the consolidated figure the corporate lenders are exposed to and how the company reports its own covenant: leverage under the Credit Agreement was 2.7 times at 2026-09-30 against a 4.75 times maximum, undrawn revolver capacity was USD 1,160.5 million, and WEX Bank's total capital ratio was 13.01% against a 10.00% well-capitalized level. Against that, EBITDA here is calculated rather than issuer-defined, the covenant definition is not printed, revolver availability depends on covenant compliance, and the cash is mostly held by WEX Bank. The view changes if the executed Credit Agreement shows that the covenant EBITDA adds back items beyond those used here, which would explain the gap between 2.7 times and the calculated figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt service coverage is thin on the cash-paid measure: EBITDA covered supplemental cash interest 2.98x in FY2025 against 3.72x in FY2023, falling because cash interest paid rose by USD 85.7 million while EBITDA rose by USD 71.7 million. Cash interest paid exceeds accrued financing interest by about USD 93.0 million, close to the USD 109.0 million of operating interest that EBITDA already deducts, which suggests it includes bank funding interest although the filing does not say so. The cover on accrued financing interest of 4.14x is therefore the better indicator of what the corporate debt costs, and it too has declined from 4.51x. Interim cash interest is not printed, so no cover is stated at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity depends on funding markets as much as on cash. The revolver has USD 1,160.5 million undrawn, but WEX Bank's FHLB capacity is only USD 14.3 million after advances of USD 1,425.0 million and its federal funds lines are uncommitted. Deposits of USD 6,180.5 million, of which HSA deposits are USD 4,758.0 million, are a non-debt funding source that finances receivables and securities; a loss of depositors or of FHLB collateral capacity would force the group to draw the revolver or shrink receivables, and the revolver is only available while the covenants are met. Nine-month operating cash flow of negative USD 419.6 million reflects receivable growth from higher fuel prices and is financed by deposits and borrowings, not by weaker earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Corporate refinancing falls outside the next twelve months apart from scheduled term loan amortization of about USD 63.4 million a year. The nearest corporate maturity is in 2028: the Term B-2 Loans of USD 1,364.0 million fall due on 2028-04-01 and, if the 91-day rule in the Credit Agreement note applies, the Term A-1 Loans and revolver would fall due on 2028-01-01 rather than 2029-05-10. The bank funding lines roll far more often: participation debt expires in December 2026 and the securitization facilities in April and October 2027, and each depends on its counterparty renewing it. A downside would begin with lower fuel prices, which cut Mobility payment processing and late fee revenue and take away the fuel price benefit of about 3 percentage points to Mobility's adjusted operating margin that the company cites for 2026; lower EBITDA then lifts leverage while the fixed corporate interest bill is unchanged. The observable tests are the average fuel price, the leverage ratio the company reports each quarter, and the renewal of the securitization and participation lines.

fields.value: Business and governance review of WEX Inc. (issuer id wex-1309108) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, transactions and new debt, governance, shareholder behaviour and capital allocation of the listed group, using the five supplied filings and the source readiness findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: WEX is a listed, bank-funded payments group with medium governance risk for creditors: the board has returned large amounts of capital through buybacks, partly funded with new debt, while earnings swing with fuel prices and depend on a regulated bank subsidiary. Buybacks of USD 2,016.1 million from 2023 to September 2026 cut shareholders' equity to USD 1,152.1 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No controlling shareholder or sponsor is named in the supplied filings, and the shareholder register and the terms of the May 2026 cooperation agreement are not established, so the willingness to curb buybacks if earnings fall cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a three-segment payments platform in which Mobility supplies more than half of revenue and moves with the fuel price. Mobility was 54.46% of revenue in the nine months to September 2026 against 52.09% in FY2025, and the company attributes USD 119.0 million of the USD 161.3 million rise in Mobility revenue to higher fuel prices, which is 73.78% of that growth while gallons processed slipped. Revenue, receivables and the funding they need therefore rise and fall with the fuel price, which is a source of earnings volatility rather than of contracted cash flow.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The bank subsidiary is the credit-relevant feature of the structure. WEX Bank funds receivables with deposits, FHLB advances and federal funds and holds the HSA deposits behind the Benefits segment: short-term deposits were USD 6,180.5 million at 2026-09-30, of which USD 4,758.0 million were HSA deposits, and restricted bank net assets were about 38% of consolidated net assets at 2025-12-31. A large part of group assets therefore sits behind regulatory dividend limits, so parent creditors rely on dividends from WEX Bank and on cash outside the bank. The FDIC consent order on compliance management, issued on 2023-09-20, ended on 2026-10-15, which removes a constraint on the bank.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation favours shareholders over deleveraging and has been partly debt-funded. The 2025 tender offer paid USD 750.0 million for shares and was financed mainly by USD 1,000.0 million of new debt, a USD 450.0 million Term B-3 and USD 550.0 million of senior notes; buybacks of USD 801.6 million in FY2025 exceeded adjusted free cash flow of USD 638.0 million, while nine-month 2026 buybacks of USD 261.8 million were covered 1.92x. A new USD 1,000.0 million program announced on 2026-05-14 had USD 740.0 million left at 2026-09-30. Equity fell from USD 1,820.6 million at the end of FY2023 to USD 1,152.1 million, leaving less loss-absorbing capital beneath the debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership gives creditors little to work with. There is no sponsor, and the one holder the filings describe as having a board nomination right, Warburg Pincus, sold all its shares and had its USD 310.0 million of convertible notes bought back at 119% of par in 2023, a USD 70.1 million loss on extinguishment. Part III information on current holders and the board is incorporated by reference and not supplied. In 2026 an activist nominated four directors and a proxy contest ended in the second quarter, with a cooperation agreement whose terms are not supplied, so shareholder pressure is a live driver of capital return without a visible counterweight in creditor terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting is good enough to monitor but not to establish creditor rights. Both annual reports carry audit opinions that the statements present fairly, controls over disclosure were effective at 2025-12-31, and the quarterly report states covenant compliance with a leverage ratio of 2.7x against a 4.75x maximum. Covenant definitions, guarantors and collateral are only summarised, so lender control, the capacity for restricted payments and the springing maturity rules cannot be confirmed from the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium risk reading is that no dividend has been declared since 2005, covenant leverage was 2.7x against a 4.75x maximum, the bank's regulatory order has ended, and the supplied filings show no covenant waiver. Nine-month 2026 buybacks were covered 1.92x by adjusted free cash flow, against 1.72x in FY2023, and no supplied filing shows an amendment that tightened creditor terms. Event risk from a leveraged takeover is also limited, because acquiring 25% of the voting stock confers regulatory control of the bank and needs prior approval, and the senior notes can be put at 101% on a change of control. The view would improve if the executed Credit Agreement shows restricted-payment limits that bind before corporate leverage rises, or if buybacks stay within adjusted free cash flow. It would worsen if a further tender offer is financed with new debt as in 2025, when buybacks covered only 0.80x of adjusted free cash flow, or if the cooperation agreement commits the company to larger returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: WEX issued new debt in March 2025 to fund shareholder returns, not an acquisition: the Seventh Amendment on 2025-03-06 added a USD 450.0 million Term B-3 due 2032-03-06 and the company placed USD 550.0 million of senior unsecured notes at 6.5% due 2033-03-15, with proceeds used primarily to fund the USD 750.0 million tender offer that closed on 2025-03-31 and to repay revolver borrowings. Earlier amendments in 2024 repriced the term loans, raised revolver commitments to USD 1.6 billion and extended maturities, and in 2026 no new debt issue appears in the supplied filings. The one operating transaction is the bp co-branded fleet card program, an asset acquisition for which USD 58.6 million was advanced in 2025 and USD 23.0 million for receivables was paid in the second quarter of 2026. Creditors should read the 2025 financing as raising corporate debt by USD 1,000.0 million for a distribution, partly offset by longer maturities.

Countervailing evidence is the 2.7x covenant leverage ratio and the termination of the FDIC order. Further analysis requires the executed debt documents and the proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for WEX Inc. (issuer id wex-1309108) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the consolidated group's business profile, financial profile, liquidity, refinancing, financial policy and downside path, built on the five supplied filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: WEX has an adequate but leverage-tolerant credit profile: three fee-earning segments and a committed revolver support the debt, while buyback-driven borrowing, fuel-price swings and dependence on a regulated bank leave creditors with stable operations but little deleveraging. Consolidated debt is 4.85x calculated EBITDA for the last twelve months and 3.20x on corporate debt alone, against a reported covenant ratio of 2.7x and a 4.75x maximum.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view is bounded by two gaps: WEX states no EBITDA, so the ratios rest on a calculated figure, and the executed debt documents are not supplied, so covenant headroom cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are large and fee-based but move with the fuel price. Calculated EBITDA was USD 995.0 million in FY2025 on revenue of USD 2,660.8 million, a 37.39% margin, and USD 1,097.8 million over the last twelve months to 2026-09-30. Mobility is 54.46% of nine-month 2026 revenue, and USD 119.0 million of its USD 161.3 million revenue growth came from higher fuel prices, so recent growth is price rather than volume and could reverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high on the consolidated measure and moderate on the corporate cut, and the consolidated figure has risen since FY2023. Total debt to EBITDA was 4.19x at the end of FY2023, 4.88x at the end of FY2025 and 4.85x at 2026-09-30, with net debt to EBITDA of 4.31x; excluding the bank and securitization funding of receivables, corporate debt was 3.20x. Creditors of the credit agreement and notes should anchor on the corporate cut while recognising that EBITDA still includes bank earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt service cover is the thinnest metric and has fallen. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.98x in FY2025 against 3.72x in FY2023, and covered accrued financing interest 4.14x in FY2025; the cash-paid measure is conservative because it appears to include interest on bank funding that EBITDA already deducts. Interim cash interest is not printed, so no cover is stated at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate on paper but rests on counterparties. The revolver had USD 1,160.5 million undrawn at 2026-09-30 and cash was USD 593.2 million, of which USD 463.0 million sat in WEX Bank, whose FHLB capacity was only USD 14.3 million and whose federal funds lines are uncommitted. The revolver is available only while the covenants are met, so a covenant breach would remove the main committed buffer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing is a 2028 event, inside 500 days of the cutoff. The Term B-2 Loans of USD 1,364.0 million fall due on 2028-04-01, 500 days from the cutoff, and the Term A-1 Loans and revolver fall due on 2028-01-01, 409 days away, if the early-maturity rule in the credit agreement note applies, or on 2029-05-10 on the annual report's schedule. WEX placed new notes and term loans in March 2025, so market access is demonstrated, but the maturity outcome depends on leverage then.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_wex-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 190; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the main constraint. Buybacks of USD 2,016.1 million since 2023 include USD 801.6 million in FY2025, which was 0.80x of adjusted free cash flow of USD 638.0 million and was funded in part by new debt, while nine-month 2026 buybacks were covered 1.92x. USD 740.0 million of authority remains, and equity of USD 1,152.1 million was 7.11% of total assets. Financial foundation shows corporate debt rose by USD 452.5 million over FY2025; Business & governance describes the March 2025 debt as raising corporate debt by USD 1,000.0 million, which is the gross issue, and the net rise was smaller because the same proceeds repaid revolver borrowings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_wex-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 119, 171, 187–188; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 19, 56, 61; calculation C4; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The bank is both the funding advantage and the structural risk. Short-term deposits were USD 6,180.5 million, restricted bank net assets were about 38% of consolidated net assets, and WEX Bank's total capital ratio of 13.01% sat above the 10.00% well-capitalized level. Parent creditors depend on dividends from the bank and on cash outside it, and any loss of deposit or FHLB funding would first hit receivable growth and then the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate but leverage-tolerant view is the covenant ratio the company reports: 2.7x against a 4.75x maximum, with adjusted free cash flow of USD 502.8 million in nine months 2026 covering buybacks 1.92x, corporate net debt of 3.10x EBITDA and a bank that is well capitalized with its regulatory order ended. If the executed credit agreement defines covenant EBITDA and permitted debt in a way that leaves wide headroom and binds restricted payments, the profile deserves a stronger view. It would weaken if a second tender offer were financed with debt as in 2025, if fuel prices fell and removed the roughly 3 percentage points of Mobility margin attributed to them, or if cash interest cover fell below its FY2025 level.

fields.value: - The ratios that anchor the view use EBITDA calculated from operating income and depreciation and amortization, so if the covenant definition adds back items the leverage conclusion could move in either direction and the 2.7x reported ratio cannot be reconciled to the 4.85x calculated one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating, market quote or peer set is supplied, so the placement of this profile among comparable leveraged issuers is a judgement from the filings alone and is not tied to market pricing or agency views.

fields.value: - The maturity ladder is drawn at the end of FY2025 and interim cash interest is not printed, so the refinancing timeline and the cover at 2026-09-30 rest on year-end data and on the last twelve months of accrued rather than paid interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit strengths are scale, a diversified fee base, earnings that held through FY2023 to FY2025 and policy restraint on dividends. Revenue was USD 2,660.8 million with no customer above 10 percent, no segment above 55% of nine-month revenue, calculated EBITDA between USD 923.3 million and USD 1,007.6 million in the three fiscal years, and adjusted free cash flow of USD 638.0 million in FY2025 and USD 502.8 million in nine months 2026. No dividend has been declared since 2005 and covenant leverage was 2.7x against a 4.75x maximum.

fields.value: The credit weaknesses are leverage tolerance, fuel-price dependence, bank dependence and thin interest cover. Buybacks exceeded adjusted free cash flow in FY2025 and were partly debt-funded, Mobility revenue growth is mostly price, restricted bank net assets are about 38% of consolidated net assets, and cash interest cover fell to 2.98x. The covenant definitions, guarantors and collateral are not established, and no rating or market evidence is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: WEX is a payments group whose cash flows are transaction-driven, not contracted, so debt service rests on volume, price and credit performance. Mobility processes fleet fuel and related payments, Benefits administers health savings accounts and invests the deposits, and Corporate Payments earns interchange and network incentives on virtual card payments; the group funds the receivables it creates through WEX Bank. That model gives visibility through many small customers with none above 10 percent of revenue, but it ties revenue and working capital to fuel prices and to funding markets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: WEX is a listed company with no sponsor, 12 holders of record and no controlling holder named in the supplied text, and with a wholly owned Utah industrial bank that holds the deposits. Debt sits at three levels: the credit agreement and notes at the parent, securitization vehicles with no recourse to the parent, and bank-level funding. Parent creditors face structural subordination to bank depositors for the bank's assets, and about 38% of consolidated net assets are restricted by bank dividend rules.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable in structure but cyclical in amount. Payment processing revenue follows dollars of fuel purchased and the net processing rate fell to 1.20% in nine months 2026 from 1.32% as fuel prices rose, because part of the fee is fixed; late fees and factoring add finance fee revenue that grows with receivables. Benefits revenue is more recurring, with SaaS accounts and custodial investment income, and Corporate Payments depends on network incentive pricing agreed in a 2025 contract amendment. A fall in fuel prices would cut Mobility revenue and receivables together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are partly variable with volume and partly fixed, which is why margin moves with the fuel price. Mobility segment adjusted operating margin was 42.52% in nine months 2026 against 39.60% a year earlier and the company attributes about 3 percentage points to fuel prices, while provision for credit losses and operating interest rise with receivables. Stock-based compensation also rose because performance awards track the fuel-driven results, so part of the margin gain is paid out to employees.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low and conversion from EBITDA to adjusted free cash flow is high on the company's own definition. Purchases of property, equipment and software were USD 140.6 million in FY2025, and adjusted free cash flow was USD 638.0 million against calculated EBITDA of USD 995.0 million, although adjusted free cash flow includes net funding activity from deposits and borrowings and is not cash after debt service. Reported operating cash flow is not a guide, because rising receivables funded by deposits and borrowings drove nine-month 2026 operating cash flow to negative USD 419.6 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry and buyer power limit pricing while the bank funding advantage and network coverage defend it. Competitors named in fleet payments include Corpay, U.S. Bank Voyager, Radius, DKV and Edenred, and WEX's closed-loop network covers more than 90 percent of U.S. fuel sites; fuel retailers and partners hold bargaining power over interchange and program terms, and the company's cost of funds through WEX Bank is its stated edge. For creditors the force that matters most is partner programs such as bp, whose economic terms are not disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory and economic factors are credit drivers here. Bank regulation matters because the industrial bank exemption, FDIC supervision and dividend limits govern funding and cash movement, and a loss of the exemption could force a divestiture or create a credit agreement default; the economic driver is the fuel price. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: scale in fleet payments, a captive bank and fee diversification across three segments. Weaknesses: leverage tolerance, fuel-price dependence and reliance on short-term bank funding. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: sustained buybacks within free cash flow, extension of the 2028 maturities and a covenant definition with wide headroom. Threats: a fall in fuel prices, loss of deposit or FHLB funding, regulatory change to the industrial bank exemption and a further debt-funded distribution.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and diversification are average to strong because three segments each earn fees and none exceeds 55% of nine-month revenue, margin stability is average because Mobility margin includes a fuel price benefit, free cash flow stability is average because adjusted free cash flow includes bank funding movements, liquidity is average because it rests on a conditional revolver and uncommitted bank lines, access to capital markets is average to strong on the 2025 issuance of notes and term loans, and financial policy is weak to average because buybacks were partly debt-funded. The trend is stable earnings with rising leverage, and the key missing datapoints are covenant definitions, a market view and interim cash interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are higher fuel prices raising Mobility revenue, growth in average HSA custodial cash assets of 11.39% year on year and the end of the FDIC order, and the headwinds are the reversal risk on fuel prices, continued buybacks and the approach of the 2028 maturities. Over three to five years the question is whether WEX holds corporate leverage near the level of FY2023 to FY2024 while returning capital, and the covenant ratio and refinancing terms in 2027 will show it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A fuel price decline is the initiating condition. It cuts Mobility payment processing and late fee revenue first and removes the fuel price benefit of about 3 percentage points to Mobility segment adjusted operating margin, then lowers EBITDA while cash interest stays fixed; leverage rises and cover falls from 2.98x. Receivables shrink and release working capital, which softens the cash effect, but a smaller receivables book also reduces deposit and FHLB funding need and bank earnings on the portfolio. Management can slow buybacks, which are discretionary, and has USD 1,160.5 million of revolver capacity, so resilience looks sufficient to avoid distress unless the covenant fails; the observable triggers are the average fuel price, the reported leverage ratio and renewals of the bank funding lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, WEX presents an adequate business profile supported by fee-based scale, a funding bank and a committed revolver, but credit quality is constrained by debt-funded shareholder returns, fuel-price dependence and reliance on a regulated subsidiary. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because adjusted free cash flow exceeded buybacks in nine months 2026. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on corporate leverage when the 2028 loans come due. The primary downside path is a fuel price fall that cuts EBITDA while buybacks and bank funding costs continue. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, covenant EBITDA, a market view and interim cash interest. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: debt-funded shareholder returns.
